history.dynasty: Hoysala Empire, with later Vijayanagara-period renovation
history.period: Built c. 1223-1224 CE by Polalva, a commander and minister of Hoysala King Vira Narasimha II; additions made in 1268 CE by Soma, a commander of King Narasimha III; extensively renovated during the Vijayanagara period
history.summary: Harihareshwara Temple is a 13th-century Hoysala temple at Harihar (CSV town 'Davangere' is WRONG - the temple is in the town of Harihar, about 14 km from Davangere city, in Davangere district). Built c. 1223-1224 CE by Polalva, a commander and minister of the Hoysala king Vira Narasimha II (with additions in 1268 CE by Soma under Narasimha III), it stands on the banks of the Tungabhadra river and is protected as a monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India. The presiding deity Harihara is the rare combined form of Vishnu (Hari) and Shiva (Hara): the idol's right vertical half is Shiva holding a trishula with ascetic hair, and the left half is Vishnu with chakra and crown. According to legend, the demon Guhasura obtained a boon from Brahma that neither Hari nor Hara could kill him singly; Vishnu and Shiva therefore took the fused form of Harihara, descended at nearby Kudalur (confluence of the Tungabhadra and Haridra rivers), and killed him - the place was called Guharanya Kshetra, and the town takes its name from the deity. Harihar is also known as Dakshina Kashi. The temple is an example of Hoysala architecture in soapstone with a staggered square plan, lathe-turned pillars, and several old Kannada inscriptions and hero stones on its premises.

name: Harihareshwara Temple
town: Harihar (CSV town 'Davangere' is WRONG - the temple is in the town of Harihar, about 14 km north of Davangere city, in Davangere district, on the banks of the Tungabhadra river)
town_description: Harihar (Harihara) is a city and taluk headquarters in Davangere district, central Karnataka, situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra river about 275 km north of Bengaluru and 14 km from Davangere - the two are called 'twin cities'. It is known as Dakshina Kashi and the 'Industrial Hub of central Karnataka', famous for the Harihareshwara Temple from which it takes its name. It is connected by road (NH-48, the Mumbai-Bengaluru highway) and railway.

travel.airport: Hubballi Airport (HBX) - about 140 km by road (verify); Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru - about 280 km (verify).
travel.road: On the Shimoga-Harihar Road / NH-48 corridor; about 16 km from Davangere, 1.5 km from Harihar bus stand; frequent KSRTC buses ply between Harihar and Davangere.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (winter/pleasant season) is the best time to visit; a road next to the temple leads to the Tungabhadra river, and the site can have uneven/slippery ground.
